tools.name: request_magic_link
tools.description:
Request a free API key by email

Step 1 of self-serve signup — no key required. Sends a one-time link to `email`; always returns 202 with the same accepted:true body whether or not that address already has a key (prevents account enumeration).

tools.name: get_event
tools.description:
Get a single event by ID

404s if the event doesn't exist, is unpublished, is beyond your tier's archive window, or was soft-deleted — never distinguishes which, to avoid leaking data existence beyond what the tier allows. Over MCP the X-Api-Key header is optional (free tier without it).

### Respon

tools.name: search
tools.description:
Semantic search over events (Pro+)

Natural-language query embedded and ranked by cosine similarity against published events — not a keyword/text match. Each result is a normal event object plus `relevance_score` (0-1). Requires Pro tier or above; free-tier keys get 403 with an upgrade_url.

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "request_magic_link" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

evidence.snippet: Request a free API key by email Step 1 of self-serve signup — no key required. Sends a one-time link to `email`; always returns 202 with the same accepted:true …

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: request_magic_link, list_events, get_event, search · Private data: request_magic_link, taxonomy · Public sink: request_magic_link.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: request_magic_link, list_events, get_event, search · Private data: request_magic_link, taxonomy · Public sink: request_magic_link

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "list_events" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
